answer: In agent economies resisting Sybil attacks, each identity forms a vertex in a transaction graph. Real agents cluster densely via repeated useful interactions, while attacker-created fakes form isolated islands. These islands hit a utility nadir: the continuous staking and maintenance cost for each low-degree vertex quickly exceeds any disproportionate influence the attacker hoped to gain, as rewards and voting power scale with proven connectivity and contribution rather than mere multiplicity.
